key_insight: Medical vision-language models recognize CT findings better in diagnostic Q&A than in free-form reports; DeCAD narrows this diagnosis-to-report gap.
clinical_relevance: Explicitly organizing diagnosis before report writing could help reduce omitted CT findings, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Identify positive findings before drafting the report.
Organize diagnosis and description into anatomical-region tasks.
Restrict each regional task to its corresponding CT visual tokens.
evidence_signal: Across five medical vision-language models, diagnostic Q&A outperformed reporting on macro-F1; full DeCAD achieved state-of-the-art performance on CT-RATE and Merlin.
watch_item: Regional visual decomposition added limited gains in medical models, and benchmark improvements do not establish real-world clinical safety.
paper_title: Decompose and Describe: Narrowing the Diagnosis-to-Report Gap in 3D CT Report Generation
